summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the first condition of salah (prayer), which is the time of prayer. He uses a foundational hadith narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah about the Angel Gabriel teaching the Prophet Muhammad the correct times for all five daily prayers. Sh. Ali Mashhour explains the precise astronomical and celestial markers for each prayer time: Dhuhr begins when the sun crosses the zenith, Asr when objects cast shadows equal to their length plus the initial shadow, Maghrib at sunset, Isha when the twilight disappears, and Fajr at true dawn. He emphasizes that these nine conditions of salah must be met for prayer to be valid, and uses practical examples like placing a stick in the ground to determine the zenith's position.
